# lightdash_project (Resource)

Manages a Lightdash project with GitHub dbt connection.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create warehouse credentials first
resource "lightdash_warehouse_credentials" "bigquery" {
  organization_uuid = "xxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxx"
  name              = "BigQuery Production"
  warehouse_type    = "bigquery"
  project           = "my-gcp-project-id"
  dataset           = "my_dataset"
  keyfile_contents  = file("${path.module}/service-account-key.json")
}

# Create a project with GitHub dbt connection
resource "lightdash_project" "analytics" {
  organization_uuid = "xxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxx"
  name              = "Analytics Project"
  type              = "DEFAULT"
  dbt_version       = "v1.8"

  # GitHub dbt connection
  dbt_connection = {
    type                  = "github"
    authorization_method  = "personal_access_token"
    personal_access_token = var.github_token
    repository            = "my-org/dbt-project"
    branch                = "main"
    project_sub_path      = "/"
  }

  # Reference warehouse credentials
  organization_warehouse_credentials_uuid = lightdash_warehouse_credentials.bigquery.organization_warehouse_uuid
}

# Create a preview project
resource "lightdash_project" "preview" {
  organization_uuid = "xxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxx"
  name              = "Preview Project"
  type              = "PREVIEW"
  dbt_version       = "v1.8"

  dbt_connection = {
    type                  = "github"
    authorization_method  = "personal_access_token"
    personal_access_token = var.github_token
    repository            = "my-org/dbt-project"
    branch                = "feature/new-metrics"
    project_sub_path      = "/"
    target                = "dev"
  }

  # Preview project references upstream project
  upstream_project_uuid                   = lightdash_project.analytics.project_uuid
  organization_warehouse_credentials_uuid = lightdash_warehouse_credentials.bigquery.organization_warehouse_uuid
}

# Alternative: Create a project with inline warehouse connection
# This is useful when you want to create a project without creating a separate warehouse credentials resource
resource "lightdash_project" "analytics_inline" {
  organization_uuid = "xxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx-xxxxxxxxx"
  name              = "Analytics Project with Inline Credentials"
  type              = "DEFAULT"
  dbt_version       = "v1.10"

  # GitHub dbt connection
  dbt_connection = {
    type                 = "github"
    authorization_method = "installation_id"
    repository           = "my-org/dbt-project"
    branch               = "main"
    project_sub_path     = "/"
  }

  # Inline warehouse connection (instead of organization_warehouse_credentials_uuid)
  warehouse_connection = {
    type             = "bigquery"
    project          = "my-gcp-project-id"
    dataset          = "my_dataset"
    keyfile_contents = file("${path.module}/service-account-key.json")

    # Optional settings
    authentication_type  = "private_key"
    location             = "US"
    timeout_seconds      = 300
    maximum_bytes_billed = 1000000000
    priority             = "interactive"
    retries              = 3
    start_of_week        = 1
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `dbt_connection` (Attributes) The dbt connection configuration for GitHub. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dbt_connection))
- `dbt_version` (String) The dbt version to use (e.g., 'v1.8', 'v1.9', 'v1.10').
- `name` (String) The name of the project.
- `organization_uuid` (String) The UUID of the Lightdash organization.
- `type` (String) The type of the project. Valid values are 'DEFAULT' or 'PREVIEW'.

### Optional

- `organization_warehouse_credentials_uuid` (String) The UUID of the organization warehouse credentials to use. Mutually exclusive with warehouse_connection.
- `upstream_project_uuid` (String) The UUID of the upstream project for PREVIEW type projects.
- `warehouse_connection` (Attributes) The warehouse connection configuration. Mutually exclusive with organization_warehouse_credentials_uuid. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--warehouse_connection))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier. It is computed as `organizations/<organization_uuid>/projects/<project_uuid>`.
- `project_uuid` (String) The UUID of the project.

<a id="nestedatt--dbt_connection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dbt_connection`

Required:

- `authorization_method` (String) The authorization method. Valid values are 'personal_access_token' or 'installation_id'.
- `branch` (String) The Git branch to use.
- `project_sub_path` (String) The subdirectory path within the repository where the dbt project is located (e.g., '/' or '/dbt').
- `repository` (String) The GitHub repository in the format 'owner/repo'.
- `type` (String) The type of dbt connection. Currently only 'github' is supported.

Optional:

- `host_domain` (String) The GitHub host domain. Optional, for GitHub Enterprise.
- `personal_access_token` (String, Sensitive) The GitHub personal access token. Required when authorization_method is 'personal_access_token'.
- `target` (String) The dbt target to use.


<a id="nestedatt--warehouse_connection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `warehouse_connection`

Required:

- `dataset` (String) The BigQuery dataset name.
- `keyfile_contents` (String, Sensitive) The contents of the service account key file in JSON format.
- `project` (String) The GCP project ID for BigQuery.
- `type` (String) The type of warehouse. Currently only 'bigquery' is supported.

Optional:

- `authentication_type` (String) The authentication type for BigQuery. Valid values: 'sso', 'private_key', 'adc'. Optional.
- `location` (String) The location of the BigQuery dataset.
- `maximum_bytes_billed` (Number) The maximum bytes that can be billed for a query.
- `priority` (String) The priority for BigQuery jobs ('interactive' or 'batch').
- `retries` (Number) The number of retries for failed queries.
- `start_of_week` (Number) The start of week (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, etc.).
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) The timeout for BigQuery queries in seconds.
